stem: Prairie Systems runs private-subnet workloads in three Availability Zones and has been told that if any single Availability Zone has a problem, workloads in the other two must keep reaching the internet without interruption.

choices.text: Deploy one NAT gateway in a single Availability Zone and route all three subnets through it regardless of where each subnet lives
Deploy one NAT gateway and add a second Elastic IP address for redundancy
Deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone but keep one shared route table pointing at only one of them
Deploy a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route each subnet to its own Availability Zone's gateway

rationale: A NAT gateway is redundant only within its own Availability Zone, so each subnet needs its own Availability Zone's gateway to keep egress isolated from a failure elsewhere. Routing all subnets to one Availability Zone's gateway, however many Elastic IP addresses it holds, still ties every subnet's egress to that single Availability Zone. Deploying a gateway in each Availability Zone but sharing one route table still sends every subnet's traffic through only one of them, so the isolation is not actually achieved.
